profile.reading:
DartPoints operates a data center at 5700 North Blackstock Road in Spartanburg, South Carolina, near downtown off Interstates 26 and 85, under the company code SPA01. This facility traces its origin to Immedion, a Greenville, South Carolina-headquartered colocation provider founded in 2007 that operated eight data centers across seven markets, before DartPoints announced its acquisition of the company on March 16, 2021. DartPoints' individual facility page lists 21,400 square feet of raised floor, drawing 1.6 megawatts of utility power against a 0.8-megawatt critical IT load, cooled by 200 tons of capacity, with 5 on-site network providers. Notably, DartPoints' own South Carolina market-overview page states a smaller 7,000-square-foot data hall and 1.3 megawatts of utility power for this same facility, though the critical IT load figure of 0.8 megawatts matches between the two pages, a partial discrepancy documented here honestly rather than resolved by picking one square-footage figure over the other. That overview page also claims SOC 2 Type II and Uptime Institute Tier III Design certification for this site, not independently corroborated by the individual facility page's more general "AICPA SOC-compliant" language. As is standard industry practice, tenant identities are not publicly disclosed, and no independently confirmed opening year is available for this specific building beyond the 2021 Immedion acquisition into DartPoints' portfolio.

DartPoints markets itself company-wide as serving more than 900 enterprise customers, including universities, hospital systems, and Fortune 500 companies, and has been recognized on the Inc. 5000 list of fastest-growing private US companies in multiple recent years, including a specific recognition among the top 30 telecom firms nationally.

reading.body:
DartPoints Spartanburg publishes 0.8 MW of IT capacity. At 10 kW per rack, a common edge-colocation density, that is roughly 80 racks; at 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, it is roughly 20 racks. The arithmetic is an illustration of scale, not an operator claim. No certifications are published on the spec page read for this site, so no certification-based judgments about what workloads the campus qualifies to host can be made.

The 0.8 MW figure places this campus fourth among the four South Carolina facilities that publish a megawatt figure at all, out of 14 facilities mapped in the state. Those four facilities together publish 6.6 MW total, meaning Spartanburg accounts for roughly 12 percent of that published South Carolina figure. Most mapped facilities in South Carolina publish no capacity figure, so the statewide total visible to this site is a floor, not a census.

For a reader deciding whether this campus matters to AI, the honest answer the published data supports is: not at the scale of AI training. A facility under 1 MW sits below the threshold where large-scale GPU clusters are practical, because a single modern AI training pod of 512 accelerators can draw that entire budget on its own. The campus is sized for edge inference, regional connectivity, or enterprise colocation, none of which are disqualifying for AI at the right workload size, but it is not a candidate for the hyperscale or frontier-model training conversations this site tracks as grid-constrained.
